methodological_rigor.justification: The design is a retrospective two-center cohort with an independent external validation (n=83), feature stability screening by ICC>0.75, mRMR+LASSO selection with 10-fold CV, and hyperparameter tuning via 5-fold CV — adequate for a radiomics signature study. However, there is no a priori sample size or power calculation, and total events (IAC prevalence 44.6%) in subgroups are modest, raising overfitting concerns given 2,264 initial features reduced to 10. Clinical/semantic radiologic variables were deliberately excluded (acknowledged), and the external cohort was intentionally scanned on the same CT platforms, which limits the generalizability test the authors claim. Statistically, DeLong tests, calibration, PRC and DCA are reported with 95% CIs, but no multiplicity correction, no bootstrapped optimism correction, and only one random train/test split are reported; the 5-fold CV on the full dataset is a reasonable sensitivity check.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: This is a retrospective diagnostic/prognostic prediction model derived from a cohort with external validation — Oxford LoE 2b. The clinical question (preoperative discrimination of invasive from pre-invasive subcentimeter SSNs) is genuinely important given LDCT-driven detection and the surgical implications of lepidic vs invasive histology. However, the endpoint is pathological invasiveness rather than patient-centered outcomes (OS/PFS), the external cohort is small and from the same scanner platforms, and no prospective or decision-impact study is presented, keeping translational relevance plausible but not demonstrated.

reporting_quality.justification: TRIPOD is the applicable standard for a prediction-model study; the authors instead reference RQS (Supplementary Table 1) and cover many relevant items — participant flow (Figure 1), predictors (feature list and selection), model development (hyperparameter grids), performance (AUC/sens/spec/F1/calibration/DCA), and external validation. Gaps include no explicit TRIPOD checklist, no protocol registration, no missing-data handling statement, limited reporting of baseline table contents in text, and inconsistent figure numbering (Figure 8/9/10 labels do not match captions). No data repository, code availability, or trained-model sharing is mentioned in the manuscript as presented, so reproducibility is weak beyond the methods narrative.

novelty_literature.justification: Novelty is incremental along the empirical and population axes: the focus on subcentimeter (≤1 cm) SSNs is a somewhat underrepresented niche, and SHAP integration is applied to a radiomics-LR model with biological interpretation of top features. However, the authors themselves acknowledge directly comparable prior work (Zuo et al. 2023, Li et al. 2025) using radiomics ± deep learning for SSN invasiveness, and SHAP for radiomics is now a well-established technique rather than methodologically novel. No new feature engineering, no new modeling framework, and no new biological validation are offered — the mechanistic interpretation of SHAP features remains hypothetical and literature-anchored.

writing_presentation.justification: The manuscript is generally readable with a conventional IMRaD structure and an informative abstract that quantitatively reflects the results. However, there is notable redundancy — the paragraph describing uAI Research Portal and PyRadiomics is duplicated verbatim within the Methods, and the SHAP section introduction has broken formatting with the subheading merged into prose. Figure captions have numbering inconsistencies (e.g., Figure 8 described as 'ROC curve for ML models' in text but caption describes SHAP, Figure 9 vs Figure 10 misalignment), and minor errors appear ('bees warm plot', 'tunning', duplicated 'Third,' in limitations). Overall the science is communicated adequately but the manuscript would benefit from a thorough copyedit.

key_strengths: Independent external validation cohort included with maintained performance (AUC 0.778, 95% CI 0.673–0.862)
Rigorous feature stability screening (ICC>0.75) retaining only 16% of initial features, followed by mRMR+LASSO
Clinically pragmatic model choice (LR) with transparent SHAP global/local interpretability and biologically plausible feature narratives
Comprehensive performance reporting: AUC, calibration, PRC, DCA, DeLong comparisons, and 5-fold CV sensitivity analysis
Focus on an underrepresented clinical niche — subcentimeter (≤1 cm) subsolid nodules
key_concerns: Retrospective, two-center design with modest sample size (n=177 development; n=83 external) and no power calculation
External validation intentionally restricted to the same CT platforms, undercutting the generalizability claim
TRIPOD checklist not explicitly addressed; no data or code availability statement in the submitted text
Incremental novelty — directly comparable prior radiomics-SSN invasiveness models (Zuo 2023, Li 2025) acknowledged in Discussion
Clinical/semantic radiologic predictors excluded, limiting fair comparison against standard-of-care radiologist assessment
Figure/caption numbering inconsistencies, duplicated Methods paragraph, and copyediting lapses throughout
chief_reviewer.rationale: Methodologically competent but incremental radiomics prediction-model study with external validation and SHAP interpretability; appropriate for a tier-3 oncology venue after minor revisions addressing TRIPOD adherence, data/code availability, and copyediting of figure captions.
